observable_outcome: Two new test files under internal/domain verify all five pure-domain Safety Invariants named in docs/architecture/validation.md section 2 by exhaustive closure rather than by sampling, the package still depends on nothing outside the Go standard library and reads no database, GitHub, Provider, network or real clock, and the evidence artifact ev-v2-010-domain is registered in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json with result passed and an evidence_hash equal to the sha256 of the artifact, so that devbox run --pure -- go test ./internal/contracts is green and devbox run --pure -- make check is green at the commit that contains the registration.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Exactly two files are created: internal/domain/invariant_model_test.go and internal/domain/source_guard_test.go. internal/domain/core_test.go and internal/domain/id_test.go are byte-identical to their state at the base commit, no production file under internal/domain changes, and git status shows no file outside allowed_paths as modified, added or deleted.

A2. Invariant 1, stale or expired fencing does not advance state. invariant_model_test.go enumerates a grid of at least (fencing-token offset in {stale, exact, unissued-future}) x (result instant in {before expiry, exactly at expiry, after expiry}) x (LeaseStatus in all four values) x (ExecutionStatus in all nine values) x (ControlMode in all seven values) x (ownership mismatch in {none, lease id, increment id, runner id}) and asserts, for every combination that is not exactly (exact token, active lease, instant before expiry, running or checkpointing execution, allow mode, no mismatch), that AcceptExecutionResult and StartExecution return a non-nil error AND return an Execution that compares equal to the input including its Version field. The test asserts the enumerated case count against a named constant declared in the file.

A3. Invariant 2, no side-effect permit survives an effective stop. This is proven in three layers, each asserting its enumerated case count against a named constant. Layer L1 enumerates the full cross product of ControlMode (all seven, plus the empty string and one unknown value) x PermitKind (all nine, plus one unknown value) x revision relation (exact, lower, higher) x fence relation (ExpectedFencingToken zero, matching, mismatching) and asserts that for every stop mode (graceful-stop, immediate-stop, emergency-stop, cancel) every PermitKind whose SideEffect() is true is denied with ErrControlDenied and a decision whose Allowed() is false. Layer L2 enumerates by breadth-first search every ControlIntent sequence of length 1 to 4 over a 21-symbol alphabet (three scopes x seven modes) with strictly increasing revisions, recomputes EffectiveControl at every prefix, and asserts that whenever the effective mode is a stop mode no side-effect permit is granted for any of the nine PermitKind values. Layer L3 accumulates, over every L2 prefix, the number of Effect values that EffectFromPermit successfully constructs while the effective mode is a stop mode, including permits captured at an earlier prefix and replayed after the stop, and asserts that counter is exactly 0. The file states the closure argument in a comment: Permit's allow/deny branch reads only mode, found, revision relation and fence relation, and EffectiveControl carries no state beyond one surviving intent per scope, therefore the enumeration decides the property for command sequences of every length, not only for length 4.

A4. Invariant 3, a completed Requirement references a Stable Release. invariant_model_test.go performs breadth-first search to fixpoint over the DecideRequirement closure, applying all nine RequirementCommandKind values to every reachable Requirement state from every one of the eleven RequirementStatus values, and asserts (a) RequirementCompleted is unreachable through DecideRequirement, (b) every reached state has a zero StableSnapshot, (c) CompleteRequirementFromRelease returns ErrInvalidTransition from every status other than evaluating, (d) from evaluating it returns ErrEvidenceIncomplete for a zero-value StableReleaseProof, and (e) with a proof produced by CompletePromotionWithProof it returns RequirementCompleted with a StableSnapshot whose ReleaseID, ReleaseVersion, BundleDigest and EvidenceDigest all match the promoted candidate and are all non-zero. The reached status set and edge count are asserted against named constants.

A5. Forbidden transitions. invariant_model_test.go performs the same breadth-first closure over DecideIncrement (all twelve IncrementCommandKind values against all twelve IncrementStatus values) and asserts that the set of accepted (from-status, command, to-status) edges is exactly equal to a declared expected edge set transcribed from the transition table in docs/architecture/domain-model.md section 5, so that a newly permitted forbidden edge fails the test rather than being absorbed. Both closures also assert that a command whose ExpectedVersion does not match the current Version returns ErrStaleVersion and leaves the state unchanged.

A6. Invariant 4, a candidate with missing capability evidence is not promotable. invariant_model_test.go enumerates, for a candidate declaring three capabilities, the full product of per-capability (evidence present) x (Verified) x (Fresh) x (candidate digest agreement) crossed with RollbackEvidence and ResumeEvidence, and asserts CanPromote returns ErrEvidenceIncomplete for every combination that is not fully present, verified, fresh and digest-matching with both rollback and resume evidence, and nil for exactly that one combination. It further crosses the fully-satisfied candidate with all seven ControlMode values and asserts PromoteRelease returns ErrControlDenied under every stop mode and that CompletePromotionWithProof yields no valid StableReleaseProof in those cases. Enumerated counts are asserted against named constants.

A7. Invariant 5, no credential field exists in the domain schema. source_guard_test.go parses every *.go file in the internal/domain package with go/parser, walks every ast.StructType, and collects every declared field name together with every json struct tag name. It normalizes each to lowercase with underscores removed and fails on any match against a closed deny list containing at least password, passwd, credential, credentials, secret, apikey, privatekey, accesstoken, refreshtoken, bearer, sessioncookie, authorization, rawprompt and rawproviderout. The matcher is exercised in the same test with positive controls (Password, APIKey, ClientSecret, RawPrompt, raw_provider_output) that must all match and negative controls (FencingToken, PreviousFencingToken, ExpectedFencingToken, ContractDigest, EvidenceDigest) that must all not match, so the deny list is verified rather than trusted. The deny list deliberately excludes the bare word token; the reason is stated in a comment. The test must not scan file text for these words, because internal/domain/control.go legitimately declares PermitCredential PermitKind = "credential" as a permit-kind value and a text scan would fail on correct code.

A8. Zero database, GitHub, Provider, network and real-clock dependency, enforced mechanically. source_guard_test.go asserts from the AST that the import set of every non-test file in internal/domain is a subset of the explicit allowlist {errors, fmt, sort, strings, time}; that no file in the package, test files included, imports net, net/http, net/url, database/sql, os/exec, math/rand, crypto/rand, or any path containing cloud.google.com, google.golang.org, github.com/google or github.com/google/go-github; that the import set of test files is a subset of an explicit second allowlist which the file declares; and that no non-test file contains a time.Now, time.Since or time.Until selector expression. The test asserts the number of scanned files is at least nine and fails when the file set is empty, so a mis-written glob cannot pass vacuously.

A9. devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v ./internal/domain passes, lists every pre-existing test name from the base commit as PASS in addition to the new ones, and its measured wall time is recorded in the report and is under 30 seconds, which is the format/lint/domain feedback budget in docs/architecture/validation.md section 7. internal/domain is executed by make component-domain, component-control-plane, component-runner, component-reconciler and component-release, so all five must be reported as passing.

A10. No entropy and no clock enter the tests. Neither new file imports math/rand or crypto/rand or calls time.Now; every varied value comes from exhaustive enumeration, from an explicit table, or from the seeded linear congruential generator pattern already used in core_test.go with the seed as the loop index. Running devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/domain three times in a row produces identical output. Per docs/architecture/validation.md section 9 no result that varied between those runs may be promoted to a pass; if any run differs, stop and escalate rather than retrying.

A11. The evidence artifact .agents/v2/evidence/V2-010-domain.json validates against contracts/schemas/evidence.json and has id ev-v2-010-domain, task_id V2-010, component domain, correlation_id v2-010-domain-invariants, result passed, and an evidence_key equal to the value reported for the domain component by devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys executed at commit A with a clean working tree. task_id is the executing task V2-010 because attribution belongs to the producer of the checks, following the precedent of ev-v2-009-release-contract whose id names the verified deliverable and whose task_id names the producing task V2-040.

A12. The artifact records one check per verification argv, each with argv in devbox run --pure -- ... form, working_directory "." and an explicit timeout_seconds: the domain test run, make component-domain, go list -deps ./internal/domain (whose summary states that the transitive dependency set is standard library only, with no third-party module path), make evidence-keys, go test ./internal/contracts, make ownership and make check. Each summary states the finitization claim in words: for the stop-permit check it names the enumerated case counts of layers L1, L2 and L3 and states that Permit's decision is total over its finite input relation, so the enumeration is a closure and not a sample. No summary contains a raw secret, a credential value or an unbounded output.

A13. .agents/v2/evidence/index.json gains exactly one entry, appended without reordering or altering the existing five, with id ev-v2-010-domain, task_id V2-010, component domain, result passed, release_eligible false, path .agents/v2/evidence/V2-010-domain.json and evidence_hash equal to the lowercase hex sha256 of the artifact file bytes. devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts is green, which includes TestActiveEvidenceIndex (bijection between the evidence directory and the index, schema validation of the artifact, recomputation of evidence_hash, and existence of the .agents/v2/task-state/V2-010.json referenced by task_id) and TestTaskPacketsValidate. Registration in the index with a matching hash and a green ledger test, not a passing domain test, is the definition of done for this Work Order.

A14. Two-commit checkpoint, pushed one at a time. Commit A contains only the two test files. The domain evidence key is read after commit A exists. Commit B contains only the evidence artifact and its index entry. Each commit is pushed alone and only after the parent commit's v2 selective CI run is green on GitHub, because scripts/verify-parent-ci.sh requires a successful attestation on the parent and two commits pushed back to back fail spuriously on the second (docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 10).

A15. Post-commit revalidation. devbox run --pure -- make check is executed and green AFTER commit B exists, not before, and that fact is recorded in the corresponding evidence check summary. gitleaks git scans committed history only, so a make check run while the artifact was still uncommitted would not have scanned the 64-hex evidence_key the artifact contains (docs/architecture/validation.md section 11, docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 10).

A16. Supersession of V2-007 is preserved. The completion report states explicitly that V2-010's complete transition must keep V2-007 in both input_refs and output_refs, because docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 6 defines a failed task as superseded only when a complete task references it from repair_of or input_refs, and if that reference is lost V2-007 stays an unsettled failed dependency and gate rule G4 blocks M1 gate V2-011 permanently. The transition itself is written by the coordinator; the implementer must not edit any file under .agents/v2/task-state/.

A17. No unrequested change of scope. No existing evidence artifact, task-state file, M0 aggregate attestation, packet, schema, document, Makefile target or ci/components.json entry is modified. If any enumeration reveals a genuine Safety Invariant violation in production domain code, stop immediately, leave the failing test in place, do not modify production code, and escalate with the failing case printed; a production fix is a different Work Order.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree. Export PATH=/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin:$PATH before any devbox invocation, and judge every run by its verdict line in the output, never by the exit code, because devbox run returns an unreliable status.

Add tests only. Do not modify, reformat or refactor any production file under internal/domain, and do not rewrite the existing tests in core_test.go or id_test.go; the measured baseline is 16 passing tests including three deterministic model-based sequences, and re-implementing them produces no new evidence.

Determinism rule: no math/rand, no crypto/rand, no time.Now, no environment variable, no file outside internal/domain, no network, no subprocess. Sequence generation is exhaustive enumeration, an explicit table, or the seeded LCG pattern with the seed as the loop index.
Every exhaustive loop asserts both an outcome per case and the total enumerated case count against a named constant, so a later narrowing of the space fails instead of silently passing.

Keep the whole internal/domain package under the 30-second domain feedback budget; five component targets execute it. Bound the intent-sequence closure at length 4 over a 21-symbol alphabet unless a measurement justifies otherwise.
English identifiers, comments and evidence summaries in the machine artifacts; the completion report to the coordinator in Japanese.

Rollback procedure: the whole change is two new test files plus one evidence artifact plus one appended index entry. To revert before commit A, delete internal/domain/invariant_model_test.go and internal/domain/source_guard_test.go and confirm devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/domain reports the baseline 16 tests. To revert after commit A, git revert commit A; nothing else depends on it because no production file changed and no manifest changed. To revert after commit B, git revert commit B first (removing the artifact and the index entry together, since TestActiveEvidenceIndex enforces the bijection and would fail on a half revert), then git revert commit A. The domain evidence key returns to its pre-change value automatically because it is derived from tracked file content.

Escalation condition 1: an enumeration finds a genuine Safety Invariant violation in production domain code. Stop, do not fix, report the failing enumerated case, and escalate to tech_lead and product_orchestrator. Do not consume the second retry attempt on an unplanned production change.

Escalation condition 2: satisfying an acceptance criterion appears to require touching a prohibited path (production domain code, ci/components.json, the Makefile, contracts/schemas, or any existing evidence or task-state file). Stop and escalate with the specific criterion and the specific path; do not widen the allowed paths unilaterally.

Escalation condition 3: the domain package cannot be held under 30 seconds while still closing the enumerated space. Report the measured time and the space size and escalate the budget-versus-coverage tradeoff rather than silently shrinking the enumeration or silently exceeding the budget.

Escalation condition 4: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/domain produces different output across repeated runs on the same commit. Escalate immediately; docs/architecture/validation.md section 9 forbids promoting such a result to a pass, and a retry must not erase the first observation.

Escalation condition 5: make check fails after commit B for a reason outside the two test files and the evidence artifact (for example a spurious parent-CI attestation failure or a pre-existing defect such as the known .github/workflows/deploy.yml action pin). Report the failure verbatim and escalate; do not fix an unrelated defect inside this task.

Retry budget is two attempts with two remaining. V2-010 is the successor of the exhausted V2-007, so a first failure leaves exactly one attempt: on a failure, report the measured cause before retrying, and if the cause is a scope question rather than an implementation defect, escalate instead of retrying.
